study type: secondary analysis of a pilot randomized controlled trial
exposure: single-nucleotide polymorphisms (COMT rs6269, rs4633, rs4818, rs4680, OXTR rs2254298, OXTR rs53576)
cohort: Sixty breastfeeding women were recruited from two hospital settings after birth.
finding: Women with the minor allele OXTR rs53576 reported 8.18-fold higher breast and nipple pain severity over time, and enhanced pain sensitivity (mechanical detection threshold and windup ratio) also predicted higher pain.
